newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO QUADRUPLE MOBILE PHONES BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO QUADRUPLE MOBILE PHONES BY 2000.

text.p: One in five Hungarians is likely to have a mobile telephone by the end of the century, quadrupling the current rate, Andras Sugar, CEO of the mobile telephone service firm Westel 900 GSM Rt said on Thursday.

Sugar was quoted by the news agency MTI as saying that Hungary, a country in transition from a communist-type system to a market economy, already has more mobile phones than France, Greece, Spain or Portugal in proportion of citizens.
He added that the operators of mobile telephone networks will have 500,000 subscribers in Hungary by the end of this year, 700,000 in 1997 and two million by 2000.

Westel 900, owned by the Hungarian telecommunication giant Matav, U.S. West and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), has invested 35 billion forints in Hungary and plans to spend the same amount for developments by 2000, Sugar said.
